question.text: A penalty for insider trading under SEBI Act can be:

answer.text: A monetary penalty of Rs. 25 crore or three times the profit made, whichever is higher, along with possible criminal prosecution
Only a warning for first offence
Penalty imposed only on the company, not individuals

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI Act framework, insider trading attracts a substantial monetary penalty — broadly Rs. 25 crore or three times the amount of profit made (or loss avoided), whichever is higher — and may also be pursued through criminal prosecution under the SEBI Act. The combination of a high statutory cap, profit-multiple computation, and possible prosecution is intended as a strong deterrent. The Trap: Capping the penalty at Rs. 5 lakhs, treating first offences as warning-only, or limiting liability to the company alone would dramatically understate the actual deterrent. Individuals are squarely within scope. Note: The specific Rs. 25 crore / three-times-profit penalty formula and criminal prosecution element are not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages; those pages discuss insider-trading allegations only in a grievance-category context. The framing above reflects general SEBI Act penalty knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
